narrative: OMX30 enters Friday trade in a bull regime (+7.4% vs 200-MA, MACD above signal) but faces significant headwinds from overnight US weakness and overbought technicals. The S&P 500 and Dow's sharp declines (-1.52%, -2.19%) signal risk-off rotation despite VIX compression (-4.26%), while US 10Y yields surge to 19-year highs (4.622%) creating a bifurcated impact: banks gain from NIM expansion, but tech and real estate face DCF compression. Commodity strength (gold +1.63%, copper +1.56%) supports mining and industrials, yet elevated oil (+1.49%) pressures consumer spending. With Stochastic K/D at 82.4/80.7 and the index at 97% of 52W range, mean reversion risk is elevated; traders should respect 3085 support (lower Bollinger) while watching for a technical pop-and-drop pattern on any opening rally.
morningBrief: OMX30 likely opens mixed-to-flat as overnight US selloff (-1.52% S&P500) clashes with technical bull setup (+7.4% vs 200-MA). Watch 3123 (yesterday close) for initial support; break below 3085 (lower Bollinger) signals deeper retracement risk given overbought Stochastic (82.4K/80.7D). Beneficiaries: Boliden (+gold/copper), SEB/Handelsbanken (yield support at 4.622%), Atlas Copco/Volvo (USD/SEK strength). Headwinds: Ericsson/Hexagon (NASDAQ -1.74%), H&M (EUR/SEK +0.25% weakens export competitiveness on sourcing), real estate (yield spike). Key macro event: US Jobless Claims 14:30 CET—market tone suggests sensitivity to labor data. ADX 24.2 (moderate bullish DI) supports upside bias but RSI 62.93 + overbought Stochastic flag tactical resistance. Range trade 3085–3150 expected.
